# Comparisons and ordering under a collation, and its propagation:
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/collation-concepts.md
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/string_functions.md
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/operators.md

WITH Words AS (SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') AS char1, COLLATE('Z', 'und:ci') AS char2)
SELECT (Words.char1 < Words.char2) AS a_less_than_Z FROM Words
=> "true"

WITH Words AS (SELECT 'a' AS char1, 'Z' AS char2)
SELECT (Words.char1 < Words.char2) AS a_less_than_Z FROM Words
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') = COLLATE('foo', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

# One collated operand collates the comparison.
SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') = 'foo'
=> "true"

SELECT 'Foo' = COLLATE('foo', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') != 'foo'
=> "false"

# The difference between sharp s and ss is secondary, so und:ci tells them apart.
SELECT COLLATE('MASSE', 'und:ci') = COLLATE('Maße', 'und:ci')
=> "false"

# Kana differences are tertiary or quaternary.
SELECT COLLATE('あ', 'und:ci') = COLLATE('ア', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT 'あ' = 'ア'
=> "false"

# Strings with different code points compare equal when their collation units do.
SELECT COLLATE('å', 'und:ci') = COLLATE('Å', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('ẞ', 'und:ci') > COLLATE('SS', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('ẞ1', 'und:ci') < COLLATE('SS2', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('b', 'und:ci') BETWEEN 'A' AND 'C'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('b', 'und:ci') NOT BETWEEN 'A' AND 'C'
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') IN ('B', 'A')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') NOT IN ('B', 'A')
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE(NULL, 'und:ci') = 'a'
=> null

SELECT COLLATE(NULL, 'und:ci')
=> null

# The value is the string itself.
SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci')
=> "Foo"

# An empty specification removes the collation.
SELECT COLLATE(COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci'), '') = 'foo'
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('Foo', '') = 'foo'
=> "false"

# A sorted query uses the collation of the values it sorts.
SELECT ARRAY(SELECT w FROM UNNEST(['Zebra', COLLATE('apple', 'und:ci')]) AS w ORDER BY w)
=> [{"v":"apple"},{"v":"Zebra"}]

SELECT ARRAY(SELECT w FROM UNNEST(['Zebra', 'apple']) AS w ORDER BY w)
=> [{"v":"Zebra"},{"v":"apple"}]

SELECT ARRAY(SELECT w FROM UNNEST(['Zebra', COLLATE('apple', 'und:ci')]) AS w ORDER BY w DESC)
=> [{"v":"Zebra"},{"v":"apple"}]

# Ignorable code points such as U+2060 do not affect the order.
SELECT ARRAY(
  SELECT fruit FROM UNNEST([
    COLLATE('oran⁠ge1', 'und:ci'),
    COLLATE('⁠orange2', 'und:ci'),
    COLLATE('orange3', 'und:ci')
  ]) AS fruit
  ORDER BY fruit
)
=> [{"v":"oran⁠ge1"},{"v":"⁠orange2"},{"v":"orange3"}]

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(w ORDER BY w) FROM UNNEST(['Zebra', COLLATE('apple', 'und:ci')]) AS w
=> [{"v":"apple"},{"v":"Zebra"}]

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(w ORDER BY r) FROM (
  SELECT w, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY w) AS r FROM UNNEST(['Zebra', COLLATE('apple', 'und:ci')]) AS w
)
=> [{"v":"apple"},{"v":"Zebra"}]

# Joins compare their keys under the collation.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST([COLLATE('a', 'und:ci')]) AS a JOIN UNNEST(['A', 'a', 'b']) AS b ON a = b
=> "2"

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST([COLLATE('a', 'und:ci')]) AS k JOIN UNNEST(['A', 'a', 'b']) AS k USING (k)
=> "2"

# Functions, operators and expressions propagate the collation of their inputs.
SELECT UPPER(COLLATE('a', 'und:ci')) = 'a'
=> "true"

SELECT CONCAT(COLLATE('a', 'und:ci'), 'b') = 'AB'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') || 'b' = 'AB'
=> "true"

SELECT [COLLATE('a', 'und:ci'), 'b'][OFFSET(1)] = 'B'
=> "true"

SELECT STRUCT(COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') AS s).s = 'A'
=> "true"

SELECT IF(TRUE, COLLATE('a', 'und:ci'), 'b') = 'A'
=> "true"

SELECT COALESCE(COLLATE('a', 'und:ci'), 'b') = 'A'
=> "true"

SELECT CASE WHEN COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') = 'A' THEN 'equal' ELSE 'different' END
=> "equal"

# BigQuery's answers. und:ci tells accents and ß from ss apart, as ICU's secondary strength does.
SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') = 'á'
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('ä', 'und:ci') = 'Ä'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('ß', 'und:ci') = 'ss'
=> "false"

# Functions that do not compare carry a collated argument.
SELECT LENGTH(COLLATE('abc', 'und:ci'))
=> "3"

SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(COLLATE('abc', 'und:ci'))
=> "\"abc\""

# A cast and a script variable drop the collation; a scalar subquery and WITH RECURSIVE keep it.
SELECT CAST(COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') AS STRING) = 'A'
=> "false"

SELECT SAFE_CAST(COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') AS STRING) = 'A'
=> "false"

DECLARE v STRING DEFAULT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci');
SELECT v = 'A'
=> "false"

DECLARE v STRING;
SET v = COLLATE('a', 'und:ci');
SELECT v = 'A'
=> "false"

SELECT (SELECT w FROM UNNEST([COLLATE('a', 'und:ci')]) AS w) = 'A'
=> "true"

WITH RECURSIVE r AS (
  SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') AS x
  UNION ALL
  SELECT x FROM r WHERE FALSE
)
SELECT x = 'A' FROM r
=> "true"
